anyOf.title: AzureDevOpsPipelineProcessor
anyOf.description: Azure DevOps Processor that migrates Taskgroups, Build- and Release Pipelines.

BuildPipelines.description: List of Build Pipelines to process. If this is `null` then all Build Pipelines will be processed.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the processor will run. Set to `false` and the processor will not run.

Enrichers.description: List of Enrichers that can be used to add more features to this processor. Only works with Native Processors and not legacy Processors.

MigrateBuildPipelines.description: Migrate Build Pipelines. A definition that already exists in the target (matched by name) is skipped and does not affect the result. A selected build pipeline that is not migrated, because it uses a task that is not installed in the target, uses a task group or variable group that was not migrated, or is rejected by the target, marks the run as failed (exit code 1).

MigrateReleasePipelines.description: Migrate Release Pipelines. A definition that already exists in the target (matched by name) is skipped and does not affect the result. A selected release pipeline that is not migrated, because it uses a task group or variable group that was not migrated, or is rejected by the target, marks the run as failed (exit code 1).

MigrateServiceConnections.description: Migrate Service Connections **secrets need to be entered manually**. A definition that already exists in the target (matched by name) is skipped and does not affect the result. A service connection the target rejects marks the run as failed (exit code 1).

MigrateTaskGroups.description: Migrate Task Groups. The versions of a task group are migrated together, lowest first. A task group that already exists in the target (matched by name) is skipped. If a version uses a task that is not installed in the target, that version and every higher version are skipped, because a version can only be created on top of the versions below it. A skipped task group, or a version the target rejects, marks the run as failed (exit code 1); task groups that already exist in the target do not.

MigrateVariableGroups.description: Migrate Variable Groups. A definition that already exists in the target (matched by name) is skipped and does not affect the result. A variable group the target rejects marks the run as failed (exit code 1).

 Use `ExportUsersForMappingConfig` to configure. The file is written to the TfsUserMappingTool UserMappingFile; display names
 shared by more than one user are written as the display name followed by the UPN in angle brackets so that each entry identifies one user.

 The lists of user can be useful, if you need tu manually edit mapping file.
 Users will be exported to file set in `UserExportFile`.

OnlyListUsersInWorkItems.description:
When true, only users that appear in the identity fields of the work items selected by WIQLQuery are exported.
 When false, all users in the source are exported.

anyOf.description: Rebuilds Test Plans and Test Suites in the target and adds the Test Cases already migrated by TfsWorkItemMigrationProcessor. Plans are matched by name and suites by title, so both must be unique. Test runs are not migrated.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the processor will run. Set to `false` and the processor will not run.

Enrichers.description: List of Enrichers that can be used to add more features to this processor. Only works with Native Processors and not legacy Processors.

FilterCompleted.description: If `true`, skips each source Test Plan whose name already exists in the target, so plans migrated by an earlier run are not processed again.

MigrationDelay.description: Milliseconds to wait before processing each Test Suite. Use it to slow the run down when the target throttles requests. `0` means no delay.

OnlyElementsWithTag.description: Only plans, suites and Test Cases whose tags contain this text are migrated. The match is a substring of the tags text, so `move` also matches `remove`. A plan or suite under the root suite that does not match is skipped with everything below it. Leave it empty or unset to migrate everything.

RefName.description: `Refname` will be used in the future to allow for using named Options without the need to copy all of the options.

RemoveAllLinks.description: If `true`, removes every link from each Test Plan the processor creates in the target. Plans that already exist in the target are not changed.

RemoveInvalidTestSuiteLinks.description: If `true`, removes links whose URI is not valid from each Test Plan the processor creates in the target, and logs each one. If `false`, such links are kept and a warning is logged, and the save can fail with "The URL specified has a potentially unsafe URL protocol". See https://github.com/nkdAgility/azure-devops-migration-tools/issues/178.

SourceName.description: This is the `IEndpoint` that will be used as the source of the Migration. Can be null for a write only processor.

TargetName.description: This is the `IEndpoint` that will be used as the Target of the Migration. Can be null for a read only processor.

TestPlanIds.description: Migrates only the Test Plans with these IDs. Pass the test plan IDs as an array, for example `[123, 456, 789]`. Leave it empty to migrate every plan selected by `TestPlanQuery`.

TestPlanQuery.description: Filtering conditions to decide whether to migrate a test plan or not. This is not WIQL: when provided, this partial query is added after `Select * From TestPlan Where` when selecting test plans. Among filtering options, `AreaPath`, `PlanName` and `PlanState` are known to work. There is unfortunately no documentation regarding the available fields. Leave it empty to select every plan.

anyOf.title: TfsWorkItemMigrationProcessor
anyOf.description:
WorkItemMigrationConfig is the main processor used to Migrate Work Items, Links, and Attachments.
 Use `WorkItemMigrationConfig` to configure.

AttachRevisionHistory.description: This will create a json file with the revision history and attach it to the work item. Best used with `MaxRevisions` or `ReplayRevisions`.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the processor will run. Set to `false` and the processor will not run.

Enrichers.description: List of Enrichers that can be used to add more features to this processor. Only works with Native Processors and not legacy Processors.

FilterWorkItemsThatAlreadyExistInTarget.description:
This loads all of the work items already saved to the Target and removes them from the Source work item list prior to commencing the run.
 While this may take some time in large data sets it reduces the time of the overall migration significantly if you need to restart.

GenerateMigrationComment.description:
If enabled, adds a comment recording the migration. The comment is added to the History of the last replayed
 revision, after that revision's own comment, rather than in a separate revision.

GenerateMigrationHyperlink.description:
If enabled, adds a hyperlink with the comment `Migrated from source` from each migrated work item to the web page of
 its source work item, in addition to the reflected work item ID and the migration comment. The link is added in the
 last replayed revision, or in a save that a re-run makes anyway, so it never adds a revision. Re-runs keep exactly one
 such link: if the source URL has changed, the old migration hyperlink is replaced. The exception is a `Migrated from source`
 hyperlink that the source work item has itself (for example because the source was itself migrated): it is copied and
 kept, so the target can then have two.

MaxGracefulFailures.description:
The maximum number of failed work items to tolerate before the run is aborted. When set to zero (the default) there is no limit: every failed
 work item is logged and recorded, the remaining items are still migrated, and the processor is reported as failed at the end with a list of the
 failed IDs. When set above zero, the run aborts once more than this number of items have failed. Use `StopOnFirstError` to stop on the first failure.

PauseAfterEachWorkItem.description: Pause after each work item is migrated

RefName.description: `Refname` will be used in the future to allow for using named Options without the need to copy all of the options.

SkipRevisionWithInvalidAreaPath.description: When set to true, this setting will skip a revision if the source area has not been migrated, has been deleted or is somehow invalid, etc.

SkipRevisionWithInvalidIterationPath.description: This will skip a revision if the source iteration has not been migrated i.e. it was deleted

SourceName.description: This is the `IEndpoint` that will be used as the source of the Migration. Can be null for a write only processor.

StopOnFirstError.description:
When true, the run stops immediately on the first work item that fails to migrate (the previous default behaviour). When false (the default),
 the failed item is recorded and the remaining items are migrated; the failed IDs are summarised at the end and the process exits non-zero.

TargetName.description: This is the `IEndpoint` that will be used as the Target of the Migration. Can be null for a read only processor.

WIQLQuery.description: A work item query based on WIQL to select only important work items. To migrate all leave this empty. See [WIQL Query Bits](#wiql-query-bits)
WIQLQuery.default: SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.TeamProject] = @TeamProject AND [System.WorkItemType] NOT IN ('Test Suite', 'Test Plan','Shared Steps','Shared Parameter','Feedback Request') ORDER BY [System.ChangedDate] desc

WorkItemCreateRetryLimit.description:
**beta** If set to a number greater than 0 work items that fail to save will retry after a number of seconds equal to the retry count.
 This allows for periodic network glitches not to end the process.

WorkItemIDs.description: A list of work items to import

FilterWorkItemsThatAlreadyExistInTarget.description:
This loads all of the work items already saved to the Target and removes them from the Source work item list prior to commencing the run.
 While this may take some time in large data sets it reduces the time of the overall migration significantly if you need to restart.

PauseAfterEachWorkItem.description: Pause after each work item is migrated

RefName.description: `Refname` will be used in the future to allow for using named Options without the need to copy all of the options.

WIQLQuery.description: A work item query based on WIQL to select only important work items. To migrate all leave this empty. See [WIQL Query Bits](#wiql-query-bits)
WIQLQuery.default: AND [Microsoft.VSTS.Common.ClosedDate] = '' AND [System.WorkItemType] NOT IN ('Test Suite', 'Test Plan','Shared Steps','Shared Parameter','Feedback Request')

WorkItemCreateRetryLimit.description:
**beta** If set to a number greater than 0 work items that fail to save will retry after a number of seconds equal to the retry count.
 This allows for periodic network glitches not to end the process.

WorkItemIDs.description: A list of work items to import

anyOf.title: TfsWorkItemTypeValidatorProcessor
anyOf.description:
Work item type validation processor. Basically it just runs the `TfsWorkItemTypeValidatorTool`
 to validate work item types. The validation is run always, even if the tool iself is disabled.
 Neither this processor, nor the tool do not perform any changes to the source or target system.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the processor will run. Set to `false` and the processor will not run.

Enrichers.description: List of Enrichers that can be used to add more features to this processor. Only works with Native Processors and not legacy Processors.

SourceName.description: This is the `IEndpoint` that will be used as the source of the Migration. Can be null for a write only processor.

StopIfValidationFails.description:
If set to `true`, migration process will stop if there are some validation errors.
 If set to `false`, migration process will continue, for example to support some other validation
 processors.
 Default value is `true`.

TargetName.description: This is the `IEndpoint` that will be used as the Target of the Migration. Can be null for a read only processor.

anyOf.title: WorkItemTrackingProcessor
anyOf.description: This processor is intended, with the aid of [ProcessorEnrichers](../ProcessorEnrichers/index.md), to allow the migration of Work Items between two [Endpoints](../Endpoints/index.md).

CollapseRevisions.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to collapse revisions into a single work item.

WorkItemCreateRetryLimit.description: Gets or sets the number of times to retry work item creation if it fails.

ExportWorkItemMappingTool.title: ExportWorkItemMappingTool
ExportWorkItemMappingTool.description:
Tool for exporting mappings of work item IDs from source to target.
 Work item migration processor uses this tool to record work item ID mappings.
 The mappings will be saved to file defined in options at the end of the migration.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

PreserveExisting.description:
Indicates whether existing mappings in the target file should be preserved when saving new mappings.
 Default value is `true`.

TargetFile.description: Path to file, where work item mapping will be saved.

FieldMappingTool.title: FieldMappingTool
FieldMappingTool.description: Tool for applying field mapping transformations to work items during migration, supporting various field mapping strategies like direct mapping, regex transformations, and value lookups.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

FieldMaps.description: Gets or sets the list of field mapping configurations to apply.

anyOf.title: FieldCalculationMap
anyOf.description: Performs mathematical calculations on numeric fields using NCalc expressions during migration.

ApplyTo.description: A list of Work Item Types that this Field Map will apply to. Use "*" to apply it to all Work Item Types. A field map with an empty list applies to no Work Item Types and never runs.

Enabled.description: Not used: every configured field map runs for the work item types in `ApplyTo`. To turn a field map off, remove it from `FieldMaps`.

expression.description: Gets or sets the NCalc expression to evaluate. Variables in the expression should be enclosed in square brackets (e.g., "[x]*2").

parameters.description: Gets or sets a dictionary mapping variable names used in the expression to source field reference names.

parsingFallback.description: Gets or sets the parsing fallback.

targetField.description: Gets or sets the target field reference name where the calculated result will be stored.

anyOf.title: FieldClearMap
anyOf.description: Clears a target field by setting its value to null, useful for removing data from specific fields during migration.

Enabled.description: Not used: every configured field map runs for the work item types in `ApplyTo`. To turn a field map off, remove it from `FieldMaps`.

targetField.description: Gets or sets the name of the target field to be cleared/set to null during work item migration.

anyOf.title: FieldLiteralMap
anyOf.description: Maps a literal (static) value to a target field, useful for setting constant values across all migrated work items.

ApplyTo.description: A list of Work Item Types that this Field Map will apply to. Use "*" to apply it to all Work Item Types. A field map with an empty list applies to no Work Item Types and never runs.

Enabled.description: Not used: every configured field map runs for the work item types in `ApplyTo`. To turn a field map off, remove it from `FieldMaps`.

targetField.description: Gets or sets the name of the target field that will be set to the specified literal value.

value.description: Gets or sets the literal value that will be assigned to the target field during migration.

anyOf.title: FieldMergeMap
anyOf.description: Merges values from multiple source fields into a single target field using a specified format template.

ApplyTo.description: A list of Work Item Types that this Field Map will apply to. Use "*" to apply it to all Work Item Types. A field map with an empty list applies to no Work Item Types and never runs.

Enabled.description: Not used: every configured field map runs for the work item types in `ApplyTo`. To turn a field map off, remove it from `FieldMaps`.

anyOf.title: FieldSkipMap
anyOf.description: Skips field mapping for a specific target field, effectively leaving the field unchanged during migration.

ApplyTo.description: A list of Work Item Types that this Field Map will apply to. Use "*" to apply it to all Work Item Types. A field map with an empty list applies to no Work Item Types and never runs.

Enabled.description: Not used: every configured field map runs for the work item types in `ApplyTo`. To turn a field map off, remove it from `FieldMaps`.

targetField.description: Gets or sets the name of the target field that should be skipped during migration, resetting it to its original value.

anyOf.title: FieldToFieldMap
anyOf.description: Maps the value from a source field to a target field directly, with optional default value substitution for empty or null values.

ApplyTo.description: A list of Work Item Types that this Field Map will apply to. Use "*" to apply it to all Work Item Types. A field map with an empty list applies to no Work Item Types and never runs.

defaultValue.description: Gets or sets the default value to use when the source field is empty or null.

Enabled.description: Not used: every configured field map runs for the work item types in `ApplyTo`. To turn a field map off, remove it from `FieldMaps`.

fieldMapMode.description: Gets or sets the mode of field mapping to be applied during migration. SourceToTarget will get data from the source system and apply it to the target. TargetToTarget will move data between the target fields.

sourceField.description: Gets or sets the name of the source field to copy data from during migration.

targetField.description: Gets or sets the name of the target field to copy data to during migration.

defaultValue.description: Gets or sets the default value to use when no mapping is found for the source field value.

targetField.description: Gets or sets the name of the target field to write mapped values to during migration.

valueMapping.description: Gets or sets the dictionary that maps source field values to target field values. Key is the source value, value is the target value.

anyOf.title: RegexFieldMap
anyOf.description: Applies regular expression transformations to map values from a source field to a target field using pattern matching and replacement.

pattern.description: Gets or sets the regular expression pattern to match against the source field value.

replacement.description: Gets or sets the replacement pattern that defines how matched groups should be used to construct the target value.

sourceField.description: Gets or sets the name of the source field to read data from and apply regex pattern matching.

targetField.description: Gets or sets the name of the target field to write the regex-transformed data to.

anyOf.title: TreeToTagFieldMap
anyOf.description: Maps work item area path or iteration path hierarchies to tags, allowing tree structures to be represented as flat tag collections.

timeTravel.description: Gets or sets the number of months to travel back in time when looking up historical area path values. Use 0 for current values.

toSkip.description: Gets or sets the number of levels to skip from the root when converting area path hierarchy to tags. For example, if set to 2, "ProjectName\Level1\Level2\Level3" would skip "ProjectName\Level1" and start from "Level2".

StringManipulatorTool.title: StringManipulatorTool
StringManipulatorTool.description: Used to process the String fields of a work item. This is useful for cleaning up data. It will limit fields to a max length and apply regex replacements based on what is configured. Each regex replacement is applied in order and can be enabled or disabled.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

Manipulators.description: List of regex based string manipulations to apply to all string fields. Each regex replacement is applied in order and can be enabled or disabled.

MaxStringLength.description: Max number of chars in a string. Applied last, and set to 1000000 by default.

TfsAttachmentTool.title: TfsAttachmentTool
TfsAttachmentTool.description: Tool for processing and migrating work item attachments between Team Foundation Server instances, handling file downloads, uploads, and attachment metadata.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

ExportBasePath.description: `AttachmentMigration` is set to true then you need to specify a working path for attachments to be saved locally.

MaxAttachmentSize.description:
`AttachmentMigration` is set to true then you need to specify a max file size for upload in bites.
 For Azure DevOps Services the default is 480,000,000 bites (60mb), for TFS its 32,000,000 bites (4mb).

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.
If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

DropPullRequestLinks.description: Pull requests are not carried by a git push, so a pull request link cannot be rewritten to the target. By default the link is kept pointing at the source pull request and a warning names the work item and pull request. Set to true to remove pull request links instead.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

Mappings.description: Dictionary mapping source repository names to target repository names. Used to update Git repository links and references in work items during migration. Keys may be a repository name ("Repo") or a project-qualified name ("Project/Repo"); the qualified form takes precedence, so repositories with the same name in different source projects can be mapped separately. A bare "Repo" key that matches repositories in more than one source project logs a warning listing them. Values may also be "Project/Repo" to pick a repository in another target project. Repositories referenced from other (or renamed) projects are resolved by repository ID and rewritten when mapped here or when the target project contains a repository with the same name.

ShouldDropChangedSetLinks.description: When set to true, changeset links in work items will be removed during migration to prevent broken links when repositories are not migrated.

VerifyTargetExists.description: When true, a commit or branch link is only rewritten to the target repository if that commit or branch exists there; otherwise the source link is kept and a warning names the work item, repository and commit. Set to false to rewrite every link without checking (the behaviour before this option existed). Pull request links are not affected; see DropPullRequestLinks.

TfsNodeStructureTool.title: TfsNodeStructureTool
TfsNodeStructureTool.description: Tool for creating missing area and iteration path nodes in the target project during migration. Configurable through TfsNodeStructureToolOptions to specify which node types to create.

Areas.description: Rules to apply to the Area Path. Is an object of NodeOptions e.g. { "Filters": ["*/**"], "Mappings": [{"Match": "^oldProjectName([\\\\]?.*)$", "Replacement": "targetProjectA$1"}] }

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

Iterations.description: Rules to apply to the Iteration Path. Is an object of NodeOptions e.g. { "Filters": ["*/**"], "Mappings": [{"Match": "^oldProjectName([\\\\]?.*)$", "Replacement": "targetProjectA$1"}] }

MigrateRootNodes.description:
By default, only child nodes in node structures are migrated. Turning this on migrates even the root node
 (default area/iteration). This is useful, when you do not have any child areas ion source, but want to migrate
 default area in source to some sub-area in target project. You have to set proper mapping for this to work.
 If after mapping the target node is still just root node (so it is not migrated under some child node),
 nothing happens – so migrating root nodes works only if the are remapped to some child node in target project.

ShouldCreateMissingRevisionPaths.description: When set to True the susyem will try to create any missing missing area or iteration paths from the revisions.

TfsRevisionManagerTool.title: TfsRevisionManagerTool
TfsRevisionManagerTool.description: The TfsRevisionManagerTool manipulates the revisions of a work item to reduce the number of revisions that are migrated.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

MaxRevisions.description:
Sets the maximum number of revisions that will be migrated. "First + Last N = Max".
 If this was set to 5 and there were 10 revisions you would get the first 1 (creation) and the latest 4 migrated.

ReplayRevisions.description:
You can choose to migrate the tip only (a single write) or all of the revisions (many writes).
 If you are setting this to `false` to migrate only the tip then you should set `BuildFieldTable` to `true`.

TfsTeamSettingsTool.title: TfsTeamSettingsTool
TfsTeamSettingsTool.description: Tool for migrating team settings including team configurations, area paths, iterations, and team-specific settings from source to target Team Foundation Server or Azure DevOps.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

MigrateTeamCapacities.description: Migrate original team member capacities after their creation on the target team project. Note: It will only migrate team member capacity if the team member with same display name exists on the target collection otherwise it will be ignored.

MigrateTeamSettings.description: Migrate original team settings after their creation on target team project

Teams.description: List of Teams to process. If this is `null` then all teams will be processed.

UpdateTeamSettings.description: Reset the target team settings to match the source if the team exists

UseUserMapping.description:
Use user mapping file from TfsTeamSettingsTool when matching users when migrating capacities.
 By default, users in source are matched in target users by current display name. When this is set to `true`,
 users are matched also by mapped name from user mapping file.

TfsUserMappingTool.title: TfsUserMappingTool
TfsUserMappingTool.description: The TfsUserMappingTool is used to map users from the source to the target system. Run it with the ExportUsersForMappingContext to create a mapping file then with WorkItemMigrationContext to use the mapping file to update the users in the target system as you migrate the work items.

EmailDomainMappings.description:
Used with MatchUsersByEmail to handle a tenant or domain change. Maps source email domains to target email domains,
 for example { "old.com": "new.com" } matches first.last@old.com to first.last@new.com. Applied when no exact email match is found.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

IdentityFieldsToCheck.description:
This is a list of the Identiy fields in the Source to check for user mapping purposes. You should list all identiy fields that you want to map.
 A configured list replaces the default list; only the listed fields are mapped, and an empty list maps none. When it is not set, System.AssignedTo, System.ChangedBy,
 System.CreatedBy, Microsoft.VSTS.Common.ActivatedBy, Microsoft.VSTS.Common.ResolvedBy and Microsoft.VSTS.Common.ClosedBy are used.

MatchUsersByEmail.description:
By default, users in source are mapped to target users by their display name. If this is set to true, then the
 users will be mapped by their email address first. If no match is found, then the display name will be used.

MatchUsersByEmailLocalPart.description:
Used with MatchUsersByEmail. When true and neither the exact email nor EmailDomainMappings produce a match, users are matched
 on the email local part (the part before @), ignoring the domain. Only a single unambiguous match is used.

ProjectCollectionValidUsersGroupName.description: This is the regionalized "Project Collection Valid Users" group name. Default is "Project Collection Valid Users".

SkipValidateAllUsersExistOrAreMapped.description: When set to true, this setting will skip a validation that all users exists or mapped

StopIfMappingTargetsDoNotResolve.description:
At startup every target value in the UserMappingFile is resolved against the identities in the target. A value that does not
 resolve, or resolves to more than one identity, would be saved as plain text with no identity behind it. When true (the default)
 the run stops before any work item is migrated; when false each problem is logged as a warning and the run continues.

UseIdentityMapDataFormat.description:
When set to true, the ExportUsersForMapping processor exports a JSON array of detailed IdentityMapData entries (Source and Target identities)
 instead of simple display name mappings, and the UserMappingFile format is detected on import so either format can be used.
 Detailed entries match work item values against the source display name or account name, ignoring case.

UserMappingFile.description:
This is the file that will be used to export or import the user mappings. Use the ExportUsersForMapping processor to create the file.
 By default the file is a JSON object mapping source display names to target display names. When UseIdentityMapDataFormat is
 enabled, the format is detected from the content: a JSON array of objects with "Source" and "Target" identities is read as
 detailed IdentityMapData, and a JSON object is read as the simple dictionary format.
 In the dictionary format a key or value may be written as the display name followed by the UPN in angle brackets to identify one of several users that share a display name.

TfsValidateRequiredFieldTool.title: TfsValidateRequiredFieldTool
TfsValidateRequiredFieldTool.description: Tool for validating that required fields exist in target work item types before migration, preventing migration failures due to missing required fields.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

Exclusions.description:
Add a list of work item types from the source that you want to exclude from validation. This is a case-insensitive comparison.
 WARNING: If you exclude a work item type that exists in the migration dataset, the migration will fail when trying to.

TfsWorkItemEmbededLinkTool.title: TfsWorkItemEmbededLinkTool
TfsWorkItemEmbededLinkTool.description: Tool for processing embedded links within work item fields, such as links in HTML fields and converting work item references between source and target systems.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

TfsWorkItemLinkTool.title: TfsWorkItemLinkTool
TfsWorkItemLinkTool.description: Tool for migrating work item links and relationships between work items, including shared steps and parameters for test cases.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

FilterIfLinkCountMatches.description: Skip validating links if the number of links in the source and the target matches!

SaveAfterEachLinkIsAdded.description:
Save the work item after each link is added. This will slow the migration as it will cause many saves to the TFS database.
 Ignored while TfsWorkItemMigrationProcessor replays revisions, because links are then saved with the revision
 where they were added or removed in the source.

TfsWorkItemTypeValidatorTool.title: TfsWorkItemTypeValidatorTool
TfsWorkItemTypeValidatorTool.description:
This tool checks if the work item types in the source system have corresponding types in the target system,
 and validates their fields and mappings.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.

ExcludeDefaultWorkItemTypes.description:
If `true`, some work item types will be automatically added to `ExcludeWorkItemTypes` list.
 Work item types excluded by default are: Code Review Request, Code Review Response, Feedback Request,
 Feedback Response, Shared Parameter, Shared Steps.
 On an inherited process these types cannot have custom fields, so they cannot hold the reflected work item ID
 field. When one of these types lacks that field, its reflected work item ID is stored in
 Microsoft.VSTS.Build.IntegrationBuild, and later runs find the work item by that field. The validator logs
 which types use this fallback.

ExcludeSourceFields.description:
List of fields in source work item types, that are excluded from validation.
 Fields excluded from validation are still validated and all found issues are logged.
 But the result of the validation is 'valid' and the issues are logged as information instead of warning.

 The key is the source work item type name. The value is list of fields' reference names which are excluded.
 You can also use `*` as key to exclude fields from all source work item types.

ExcludeWorkItemTypes.description: List of work item types which will be excluded from validation.

IncludeWorkItemTypes.description: List of work item types which will be validated. If this list is empty, all work item types will be validated.

ScanRevisionHistoryForFields.description:
If `true`, before migration starts the work items to be migrated are scanned for fields that
 have a value only in revision history: the revision was saved under another team project or work item type
 (the item was moved or its type changed), and the field is on neither the source type in the current project
 nor the target type the revision is replayed to. These values cannot be migrated, and field maps cannot read
 them. Only moved or retyped revisions are checked, but each one is loaded with a separate server request,
 so the scan can add significant time when many items were moved. It is off by default.

StopIfHistoryOnlyFieldsFound.description:
If `true` and `ScanRevisionHistoryForFields` finds history-only fields that are
 not excluded by `ExcludeSourceFields`, the migration stops before any work item is migrated.
 If `false`, the fields are logged as warnings and the migration continues.

WorkItemTypeMappingTool.title: WorkItemTypeMappingTool
WorkItemTypeMappingTool.description: Provides mapping functionality for transforming work item types from source to target systems during migration, allowing different work item type names to be used in the target.

Enabled.description: If set to `true` then the tool will run. Set to `false` and the tool will not run.
